text:
Alex Ovechkin set another record this week, passing Nicklas Backstrom for the most assists in Capitals history with his 763rd. The rest of the week was harder. This is Ovechkin's farewell season, the Lightning sent him off with custom cigars on his last trip to Tampa, and the team around him is winless in four (0-4-0), outscored 23-11.

Our numbers call the skid partly real: 48% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, in that run. Over the full season, the Caps are 10-10 with almost exactly even chances (49.9%) and have allowed about six and a half more goals than an average goalie would on those shots. Goaltending, not structure, is the gap. Their playoff chances sit around 37%.

Ovechkin and Tom Wilson are running cold, with 2 points each in the last 10 games against 4.6 and 5.3 expected. Wilson has been in the news for other reasons too, avoiding a suspension for his hit on Florida's Sandis Vilmanis, and Jakob Chychrun's hit on Ottawa's Nick Cousins has been argued about for a week. Ryan Leonard has a three-game goal streak and a maximum fine for high-sticking.

The bright spot is the Boone Jenner, Justin Sourdif and Leonard line, which has had 73% of the chances in a small sample. The Tuch, Strome and Jordan Kyrou line creates the most but is down 7-5. A save or two would change this team's mood quickly.
headline: Ovechkin's goodbye tour hits a skid
